paragraphs: Evaluating a new decision policy from previously collected data becomes difficult when the original decisions depended on information that was never recorded. This paper studies that setting in partially observable Markov decision processes. The policy being evaluated uses observable variables, while the policy that generated the data can depend on hidden variables, creating latent confounding.

The authors introduce bridge functions that connect the target policy’s value to the distribution of observed data. These functions provide the basis for new identification methods: ways of expressing the evaluation target through available observations. The paper then develops minimax estimation methods to learn the bridges rather than requiring them to be known beforehand.

Using the learned bridges, the authors construct value-based, marginalized importance-sampling, and doubly robust estimators. Their framework permits general function approximation, extending its applicability to continuous or large observation and state spaces. They investigate both finite-sample and asymptotic properties, providing a statistical treatment of policy evaluation that explicitly accommodates hidden confounding in this partially observed setting.
icml-2022-a-minimax-learning-approach-to.tldr: Learned bridge functions support off-policy evaluation with hidden confounders and large or continuous observation and state spaces.

paragraphs: ADIOS turns the choice of which image regions to hide into a learning problem. It jointly trains an image encoder and a masking function without requiring labels for this training objective. The encoder tries to produce similar representations for an original image and its masked version, while the masking function tries to make those representations differ.

These opposing objectives make masking an active part of representation learning. The masking function searches for challenging omissions, and the encoder learns to maintain agreement despite them. The authors report that the resulting masks are semantically meaningful and improve representation learning more effectively than masking schemes used in popular masked image models.

Across the reported evaluations, ADIOS consistently improves strong self-supervised methods on image classification, transfer learning, and robustness to background changes. The framework also works with convolutional networks because it does not depend on the image-patch tokenization used by Vision Transformers. This broadens where learned adversarial masking can be applied while preserving its central training objective.
icml-2022-adversarial-masking-for-self-s.tldr: ADIOS jointly learns challenging image masks and an encoder, improving self-supervised representations across the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Hierarchical variational autoencoders learn representations at multiple latent levels, but their generated images can have poor quality. This paper treats image generation as a problem of organizing information across that hierarchy. Its guiding idea is the progressive coding hypothesis: hierarchical models that perform well at progressive lossy compression should also generate high-quality samples.

The authors first examine whether conventionally trained hierarchical autoencoders already behave as effective progressive coders. Their empirical findings indicate that they do not. Having a hierarchy of latent variables therefore does not, by itself, establish that the model prioritizes information in a way that is useful for progressively reconstructing an image.

The proposed method constrains the learned representations to prioritize information beneficial for lossy compression. Applying this constraint improves the quality of generated samples in the reported experiments. The results offer further support for the progressive coding hypothesis and suggest a concrete design principle: how information is allocated within a latent hierarchy can matter for image synthesis.
icml-2022-bit-prioritization-in-variatio.tldr: Prioritizing compression-useful information within hierarchical variational autoencoders improves generated image quality and supports the progressive coding hypothesis.

paragraphs: This paper investigates whether access to randomness can let neural networks accomplish tasks with fewer neurons than deterministic networks. Its Coin-Flipping Neural Networks use amplification to obtain benefits from randomized computation. The authors establish a striking approximation result: a two-layer randomized network with a constant number of neurons can approximate membership in a d-dimensional ball to arbitrary accuracy.

For that problem, the cited requirement for a two-layer deterministic network grows exponentially with dimension. The resulting separation demonstrates a substantial representational advantage in this particular setting. A second theorem shows that almost any classification problem admits a very simple network when supplied with a sufficiently powerful generator of its weights; the generator’s strength is an essential condition.

The authors conjecture that randomized networks offer better accuracy or smaller size for most classification problems, extending beyond what their theorems establish. They also test new architectures on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100, reporting an improvement of 9.25% from their baseline. These experiments accompany the theoretical results without turning the broader conjecture into a proven universal advantage.
icml-2022-coin-flipping-neural-networks-.tldr: Randomized neural networks achieve a major size advantage for a specific approximation problem and show empirical classification gains.

paragraphs: Unsupervised domain adaptation aims to classify data in a target domain using labeled examples from a different source domain and unlabeled target examples. A common approach seeks features that hide the distinction between domains. This paper examines an alternative: contrastive pretraining on unlabeled data from both domains, followed by fine-tuning on labeled source data.

The authors find that this procedure is competitive with strong domain-adaptation methods even though its learned features retain substantial domain information. That observation challenges the idea that successful transfer must work by making representations domain-invariant. Features can remain sensitive to the domain while still supporting classification in the target domain.

The paper supplies a theoretical explanation based on separating domain information from class information within the representation. It shows that contrastive pretraining can learn features with substantial cross-domain variation and nevertheless generalize to the target. Experiments on vision benchmarks support this explanation, suggesting that organizing the two kinds of information can be sufficient without eliminating domain variation.
icml-2022-connect-not-collapse-explainin.tldr: Contrastive pretraining can support domain adaptation by separating class and domain information while retaining domain-sensitive features.

paragraphs: A backdoored language model can behave normally until a particular token sequence triggers malicious behavior. Finding that sequence through trigger inversion is difficult because text consists of discrete choices. The paper develops an optimization method for this setting, addressing the obstacle that prevents direct application of inversion techniques designed for vision models.

The method gradually lowers the temperature of a softmax function, changing the optimization landscape as the search proceeds. This process increasingly concentrates the search toward a discrete trigger, represented by a one-hot choice within a continuous convex region. A rollback mechanism can raise the temperature again to move away from local optima, exploiting their recognizability in this particular inversion problem.

The evaluation covers more than 1,600 models, approximately half with injected backdoors, across three NLP tasks, four attacks, and seven architectures. The authors report effective and efficient backdoor detection and removal, outperforming five baseline methods. The findings support dynamically changing the continuous search landscape as a practical approach to recovering discrete malicious triggers.
icml-2022-constrained-optimization-with-.tldr: A temperature-controlled optimization method recovers discrete NLP backdoor triggers and improves detection and removal in the reported evaluation.

paragraphs: Content-addressable memory retrieves a stored pattern from an incomplete or corrupted version of it. Conventional networks can recover a small collection of rich patterns almost perfectly, then suffer a sharp collapse when their storage capacity is exceeded. This paper introduces MESH, an architecture designed to replace that sudden failure with a gradual trade-off between how many patterns are stored and how much detail remains recoverable.

MESH separates the internal dynamics that stabilize memory states from the associations connecting those states to external content. Its three-part architecture uses pairwise interactions, a predetermined collection of stabilized internal states, and associations to arbitrary external patterns. The design is motivated by the brain’s entorhinal–hippocampal memory circuit.

With few patterns, MESH recovers complete information at the level of standard content-addressable memories. As more patterns are inserted, it retains partial recall of every pattern. The authors report analytical and experimental evidence that it nearly reaches the information bound set by the number of synapses for any number of stored patterns, outperforming existing CAM models.
icml-2022-content-addressable-memory-wit.tldr: MESH separates stable internal memory states from stored content, allowing recall to degrade gradually as more patterns are added.

paragraphs: Data augmentation is often explained as enlarging a training set or encouraging predictions to remain unchanged under particular transformations. This paper studies another role: changing which features a model learns during training. The focus is on learning dynamics, meaning how the model’s use of information develops as optimization proceeds.

The authors find that augmentation can change the relative importance of available features. In particular, it can make informative features that are difficult to learn more likely to be captured. They report that this effect is stronger in nonlinear models such as neural networks, making the interaction between augmentation and model structure central to the explanation.

The main theoretical contribution analyzes a two-layer convolutional neural network in a multi-view model. Additional experiments support the interpretation of augmentation as feature manipulation. Together, these results explain how augmented data can influence learning beyond the number of examples presented: it can alter the balance of information that the training process picks up.
icml-2022-data-augmentation-as-feature-m.tldr: Data augmentation can change learning dynamics so that informative but difficult features become more likely to be learned.

paragraphs: A neural network’s total parameter count need not equal the number of parameters that must adapt to a particular target function. This paper studies that distinction through approximation theory. It asks how much function-specific information must be learned when the remaining network structure and parameters can be specified separately.

For any Lipschitz-continuous function on the d-dimensional unit cube with Lipschitz constant λ, the authors construct a ReLU network with n + 2 target-dependent parameters and approximation error bounded by 5λ√d times 2 to the power −n. The bound decreases exponentially with n. They also generalize the construction to continuous functions beyond the Lipschitz case.

These are statements about intrinsic, function-dependent parameters rather than a claim that the entire network has only n + 2 parameters. The authors complement the theory with classification experiments in which only a small subset of parameters is trained. They report good results when the other parameters are predetermined or pretrained on a related problem, illustrating the practical relevance of selective adaptation.
icml-2022-deep-network-approximation-in-.tldr: Constructed ReLU networks can approximate functions accurately with few target-dependent parameters, with experiments supporting selective parameter training.

paragraphs: Ensembles of neural networks can strengthen deep reinforcement learning methods, but training many networks makes each update expensive. DNS addresses this cost by changing which ensemble members receive backpropagation at each training step. The approach retains an ensemble while selectively spending computation on a subset of its networks.

The selection mechanism uses a k-determinantal point process, or k-DPP, to sample that subset. The central intervention is therefore in the training procedure: the method does not backpropagate through every ensemble member at every step. The authors propose this sampler as a way to reduce both training time and computational expense in ensemble reinforcement learning.

They integrate DNS into REDQ and evaluate it on continuous-control tasks in MuJoCo environments. In those experiments, DNS-augmented REDQ matches baseline REDQ’s average cumulative reward while using less than half the computation measured in floating-point operations. This result shows that selective ensemble updates can preserve the reported control performance while substantially reducing arithmetic work in the evaluated setting.
icml-2022-dns-determinantal-point-proces.tldr: DNS samples ensemble members for backpropagation, matching REDQ’s reported reward with less than half its floating-point computation.

paragraphs: This paper approaches fairness by learning a representation on which optimal predictors are invariant across subgroups. The representation itself becomes the object of optimization: it should support prediction while satisfying this cross-group requirement. The authors formulate the idea as a nested optimization problem, with representation learning outside and updates to group predictors inside.

They show that the proposed objective satisfies the sufficiency rule, a fairness criterion that the abstract identifies as useful but comparatively understudied in fair learning. The nested formulation creates a computational challenge because differentiating through the inner optimization can require substantial time and memory. Addressing that cost is a central part of the method.

The proposed implicit path alignment algorithm uses the inner problem’s solution and implicit differentiation instead of following its exact optimization trajectory. The authors analyze the error gap introduced by this approach and evaluate it on classification and regression. Their experiments show consistently better trade-offs between prediction performance and the measured fairness, supporting the combination of the fairness objective and efficient optimization.
icml-2022-fair-representation-learning-t.tldr: A nested fairness objective and implicit optimization method improve reported trade-offs between prediction performance and fairness.

paragraphs: Learning a convex function appears in regression, models based on differences of convex functions, and the learning of divergences. This paper develops faster solvers for a broad range of these problems. Its approach uses a two-block alternating direction method of multipliers, with each block update available in closed form.

For convex Lipschitz regression on n examples with d features, the authors establish an iteration bound of O(n√d/ε). Accounting for the work within each iteration gives a total complexity that improves the previous stated rate when d grows more slowly than n to the fourth power. The improvement therefore comes with an explicit relationship between dataset size and dimension.

The paper also supplies related solvers for difference-of-convex regression and Bregman divergence learning. Its computational structure supports GPU use, providing another route to practical speed. In regression and metric-learning experiments, the approach runs more than 100 times faster than existing methods on some datasets while producing results comparable to the state of the art.
icml-2022-faster-algorithms-for-learning.tldr: Closed-form two-block optimization updates accelerate convex function learning, with theoretical improvements and large speedups on some datasets.

paragraphs: Minimax learning involves optimizing competing objectives, as in generative adversarial networks. When training data are distributed across clients, the optimization must also account for communication costs. This paper studies Local SGDA, a version of stochastic gradient descent–ascent that performs local updates in a federated setting.

The authors establish order-optimal sample complexity for several classes of nonconvex–concave and nonconvex–nonconcave problems. Their analysis also shows linear speedup with the number of clients in the analyzed settings. A tighter treatment improves existing convergence and communication guarantees, clarifying how efficiently local updates can solve these distributed minimax problems.

The theoretical contributions extend to centralized optimization, where the paper improves complexity results for nonconvex–PL and nonconvex–one-point-concave objectives. The authors additionally introduce a momentum-based local-update method. It shares Local SGDA’s convergence guarantees but performs better in their experiments. Thus, the paper contributes both stronger understanding of an established algorithm and an empirically improved alternative within the same guarantee level.
icml-2022-federated-minimax-optimization.tldr: Tighter analysis establishes efficient Local SGDA guarantees for several minimax classes, while a momentum variant improves experimental performance.

paragraphs: The k-center clustering problem can be expressed as a mixed-integer nonlinear optimization problem. This paper develops a practical algorithm with a guarantee of convergence to its global optimum. Its central strategy is reduced-space spatial branch and bound: the search branches only on the locations of cluster centers.

Because the branching variables are the centers, their number does not depend on how many data points the dataset contains. The authors also introduce feasibility-based bound tightening, which narrows the possible locations of centers and accelerates convergence. These choices target the size of the optimization search while preserving the global-convergence guarantee.

Results span 32 datasets. For a dataset containing 14 million samples and three features, the serial implementation reaches a 0.1% optimality gap within two hours. The paper also reports an average objective reduction of 30.4% for its global optima compared with a heuristic method. The large-dataset result illustrates a concrete certified approximation level, while the comparison shows the potential value of improving beyond heuristic solutions.
icml-2022-global-optimization-of-k-cente.tldr: Branching only on cluster centers enables globally convergent k-center optimization with strong reported results on large datasets.

paragraphs: Gradient-free optimization is useful when derivatives are difficult or impossible to obtain. Constraints make this harder, especially when there are many nonconvex restrictions defined by explicit formulas or black-box evaluations. Existing approaches can become inefficient because they evaluate every constraint or project candidate solutions onto a complicated feasible set.

The paper proposes DSZOG, a doubly stochastic zeroth-order gradient method for this heavily constrained setting. It combines momentum with an adaptive step size. The method is designed to address the computational obstacles created by numerous white-box or black-box constraints while operating without directly available gradients.

The authors prove convergence to an ε-stationary point of the constrained problem, an approximate stationarity guarantee rather than a guarantee of global optimality. They also evaluate the method in two applications, reporting better training time and accuracy than other constrained zeroth-order methods. Together, the theoretical and experimental results support its use for nonconvex problems where derivative access and constraint-handling costs are both important obstacles.
icml-2022-gradient-free-method-for-heavi.tldr: DSZOG combines gradient-free stochastic updates, momentum, and adaptive step sizes to handle nonconvex problems with many constraints.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to choose noisy function evaluations adaptively when searching for an unknown function’s optimizer. It assumes the function belongs to the reproducing kernel Hilbert space of a known kernel and has a bounded norm. These restrictions make it possible to analyze what an algorithm can learn from its queries.

Earlier worst-case analyses characterize the hardest functions in a class, but reveal less about a particular function or the benefits of easier instances. The authors derive instance-dependent regret lower bounds for algorithms whose normalized cumulative regret vanishes uniformly over the class. The result applies to several established kernelized-bandit algorithms and identifies a complexity measure associated with each individual instance.

The paper then proposes an algorithm that remains near-optimal in the minimax sense while adapting to easier instances. This joins two goals: retaining strong protection against difficult functions and exploiting favorable structure when it is present. The contribution is a more differentiated account of learning difficulty than a single worst-case rate can provide.
icml-2022-instance-dependent-regret-anal.tldr: Instance-dependent lower bounds and an adaptive algorithm distinguish easier kernelized-bandit problems while retaining near-optimal worst-case performance.

paragraphs: Comparing datasets is difficult when there is no known correspondence between their individual observations. Differences in sample count, feature count, or measurement modality make direct comparisons even less straightforward. This paper compares the datasets’ intrinsic geometric structures, using manifold learning to describe how each dataset is organized internally.

The method represents that geometry through diffusion operators, expressed as symmetric positive-definite matrices related to discrete approximations of the Laplace–Beltrami operator. Rather than comparing operator entries point by point under an assumed alignment, the authors use the geometry of positive-definite matrices. They derive a distance from a lower bound on the log-Euclidean metric.

The resulting log-Euclidean signature, or LES, supports comparisons across datasets with different sizes, dimensions, and modalities. The authors report that it captures meaningful structural differences and outperforms competing approaches across several application domains. Its contribution is a way to compare internal dataset geometry without requiring the sample-level alignment that existing pointwise approaches typically assume.
icml-2022-log-euclidean-signatures-for-i.tldr: Log-Euclidean signatures compare the intrinsic geometry of datasets without requiring known alignment between their observations.

paragraphs: Active learning reduces labeling effort by selecting informative examples rather than requesting labels indiscriminately. That selection process can also introduce unfairness. This paper asks whether an algorithm can preserve label efficiency while meeting metric-fairness requirements, making fairness part of the learning problem rather than treating selection solely as an information-gathering decision.

The analysis concerns homogeneous halfspaces, a particular class of linear classifiers, under a distribution-dependent probably approximately correct learning model. Within that setting, the authors show that fairness and efficient use of labels can be achieved simultaneously. The result establishes compatibility between the two goals for the studied class and learning framework.

The paper extends its main results in two directions. First, it shows that robustness to adversarial noise is possible, addressing a demanding noise model. Second, it shows that label complexity can improve significantly when the underlying halfspace is sparse. These extensions connect the fairness result to both difficult labeling conditions and exploitable structure in the classifier being learned.
icml-2022-metric-fair-active-learning-b3.tldr: Metric fairness and label efficiency can coexist for active learning of homogeneous halfspaces in the studied distribution-dependent framework.

paragraphs: Steerable neural networks are designed so their features transform in a controlled way when the input is rotated. Constructing such networks for three-dimensional rotations is mathematically more involved than doing so in two dimensions. This paper uses partial differential operators to represent three-dimensional filters and derive a general family of steerable CNNs.

The authors prove that the required equivariant filters satisfy linear constraints, which can be solved efficiently under various conditions. Their construction covers all common subgroups of the three-dimensional rotation group SO(3) and their representations. On this basis, they describe it, to their knowledge, as the most general available steerable CNN framework for three-dimensional rotations.

Experiments investigate both transformation behavior and task performance. The models preserve equivariance well after moving to a discrete representation and outperform previous work on SHREC’17 retrieval and ISBI 2012 segmentation with low network complexity. The findings connect the general mathematical construction to practical models that retain useful rotational structure in their implemented form.
icml-2022-pdo-s3dcnns-partial-differenti.tldr: Partial differential operators yield a broad family of rotation-equivariant 3D CNNs through efficiently solvable linear filter constraints.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning must learn from an existing dataset without exploring the environment for additional evidence. Sparse data and incomplete coverage can distort estimated action values. Pessimistic methods address this problem by making value estimates conservative, but the sample efficiency of model-free versions has received less theoretical attention than that of model-based approaches.

This paper studies pessimistic Q-learning for finite-horizon Markov decision processes. It characterizes the amount of data required under a single-policy concentrability assumption. That assumption does not require the dataset to cover the entire state–action space, making the analysis relevant to the incomplete coverage that motivates offline learning.

The authors also propose a variance-reduced version of pessimistic Q-learning and establish near-optimal sample complexity. The result shows that explicit estimation of an environment model is not required to obtain this level of sample efficiency in the analyzed setting. Pessimism and variance reduction together provide the basis for the stronger model-free guarantee under the stated coverage assumption.
icml-2022-pessimistic-q-learning-for-off.tldr: Variance-reduced pessimistic Q-learning achieves near-optimal offline sample complexity under a coverage assumption that does not require all state–action pairs.

paragraphs: Neural architecture design often lacks direct guidance from theory. This paper proposes starting with a well-performing kernel, whose mathematical structure may be easier to understand and design, and translating it into a neural network. The intended benefit is to connect principled kernel construction with the efficiency, flexibility, and feature-learning capabilities of networks.

The authors give a constructive proof for positive-semidefinite dot-product kernels. By choosing an appropriate activation function, any kernel in this class can be realized as either the neural-network Gaussian-process kernel or the neural tangent kernel of a fully connected network with one hidden layer. The activation choice is therefore sufficient for the stated kernel realization.

Numerical checks verify the construction, and experiments demonstrate its usefulness for designing finite fully connected networks. These empirical results connect the kernel correspondence to practical architecture choices. The paper’s contribution is a concrete route from a desired kernel to a network design, with the theoretical guarantee applying to the specified class of kernels.
icml-2022-reverse-engineering-the-neural.tldr: Choosing an activation function can realize any positive-semidefinite dot-product kernel as a one-hidden-layer network’s NNGP or neural tangent kernel.

paragraphs: Group synchronization requires estimating group elements from relationships that may be corrupted. This paper approaches the problem by first estimating the levels of corruption and then using those estimates to solve the synchronization task. Its method, detection and estimation of structural consistency, or DESC, is formulated as a quadratic program.

The objective uses cycle consistency: relationships around a cycle should agree with the underlying group structure. This structural information supplies evidence about corruption without requiring a good initial estimate of the group elements. The authors also describe the framework as extendable to other algebraic and geometric structures.

The formulation can tolerate corruption up to the information-theoretic bound, and under stated mild conditions its global minimum exactly recovers the corruption levels. Exact recovery is thus tied to both those conditions and the global minimum of the objective. Synthetic and real rotation-averaging experiments show competitive accuracy, providing empirical support for using structural consistency to guide robust estimation.
icml-2022-robust-group-synchronization-v.tldr: DESC uses cycle consistency and quadratic programming to estimate corruption and support robust group synchronization.

paragraphs: When unobserved confounders prevent a causal quantity from being uniquely identified, bounds can still describe the range of possible answers. Computing those bounds is often expensive. Existing nonparametric linear-programming formulations grow exponentially with the number of edges in the causal graph, quickly exceeding what available solvers can handle.

This paper shows that examining the structure of the particular causal query allows much of the linear program to be pruned. The smaller formulation makes bounds computable for substantially larger problems. For a special class of graphs and queries, the same reasoning produces closed-form bounds, including problems in which multiple confounded treatments affect an outcome.

The authors additionally propose a greedy heuristic for problems beyond the reach of the pruned linear program. They report very high-quality bounds and scalability to problems several orders of magnitude larger. These contributions provide complementary ways to make causal bounding more tractable: query-specific pruning, closed-form results in a special class, and an efficient heuristic for larger cases.
icml-2022-scalable-computation-of-causal.tldr: Query-aware pruning and a greedy heuristic make causal bounds computable for much larger problems with unobserved confounding.

paragraphs: Training each transformer size independently discards the opportunity to reuse work already performed on smaller models. This paper studies staged training, which starts small and increases model depth and width during training. Each growth operator transforms the complete training state, including parameters, optimizer state, and the learning-rate schedule, so training can continue in the larger model.

The authors identify two properties that matter when making this transition. A growth operator should preserve the loss and also preserve training dynamics, specifically the rate at which the loss decreases. Maintaining the current loss alone does not capture this second property, which concerns how effectively the model continues learning after growth.

The paper uses scaling laws to choose stage transitions when training efficiency begins to fall, seeking the schedule with the greatest compute savings. Experiments on autoregressive language models validate the growth operators and staged procedure. They show compute savings of up to 22% against a strong baseline trained from scratch, demonstrating the potential value of reusing earlier training stages.
icml-2022-staged-training-for-transforme.tldr: Growing transformers while preserving loss and training dynamics yields up to 22% compute savings in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: This paper develops an attention mechanism inspired by recurrence and sparsity in human visual attention. Called VARS, it uses recurrent connections to group related features and sparse regularization to make salient objects emerge. The mechanism is an attractor network whose activity evolves toward a stable pattern over time.

The authors express its layers as ordinary differential equations and connect the recurrent dynamics to an optimization problem. In that interpretation, attention reconstructs the input sparsely using a dictionary of templates that encode underlying data patterns. The formulation gives the attention mechanism both a dynamical description and an equivalent reconstruction-based objective.

Within this framework, self-attention appears as a special case using a single optimization step and no sparsity constraint. VARS can replace self-attention in popular vision transformers, and the authors report consistent robustness improvements across multiple benchmarks. The results support recurrent sparse reconstruction as a practical attention design while also explaining how it relates mathematically to an established mechanism.
icml-2022-visual-attention-emerges-from-.tldr: VARS formulates attention as recurrent sparse reconstruction, generalizes self-attention, and improves reported vision-transformer robustness.
